q: A senior employee finds that his junior draws higher pay in the same post solely because the junior received a financial upgradation under MACPS. The senior claims stepping up of his pay to the junior's level. The claim is:

options.A: Not admissible, because stepping up cannot be claimed against a junior's MACPS upgradation
options.B: Admissible, because both are in the same cadre
options.C: Admissible from the date the junior was upgraded
options.D: Admissible if the senior was promoted earlier than the junior

e: A MACPS-driven difference is not an FR 22 fixation anomaly, so stepping up with reference to it is not admissible.

q: An employee is promoted on 10 April 2026. He exercises no option within one month, but in June asks for his pay to be fixed from his date of next increment. The correct action is to fix his pay:

options.A: From the date of his letter in June
options.B: From his date of next increment, as now requested
options.C: Under FR 22(I)(a)(1) with effect from the date of promotion itself
options.D: At the minimum of the higher level from June

e: If no option is exercised within one month, pay is fixed under FR 22(I)(a)(1) from the date of promotion, not from a later date.

q: An employee is on deputation away from his parent cadre. Meanwhile his junior (next below him) in the parent cadre is promoted. The provision that protects the deputationist's promotion benefit in the parent cadre is:

options.D: The Next Below Rule, giving proforma fixation/promotion benefit

e: The Next Below Rule gives proforma benefit to a servant away on deputation or an ex-cadre post when his next below is promoted at home.

q: An employee has remained at the maximum of his level for two years and is granted a stagnation increment. For which purposes does this increment count?

options.A: It counts only for Dearness Allowance
options.B: It counts only for House Rent Allowance
options.C: It is a personal pay that counts for no purpose
options.D: It is treated as pay for all purposes, including pensionary benefits

e: A stagnation increment, granted after every two years at the maximum at the rate of the last increment, counts as pay for all purposes including pension.

q: An employee granted a MACPS upgradation claims the designation, duties and seniority of the higher level from the date of upgradation. The correct position is:

options.A: The claim fails; MACPS is purely financial and he remains on the same post with unchanged designation, duties and seniority
options.B: The claim succeeds; MACPS is a regular promotion for all purposes
options.C: Only the designation changes, not the seniority
options.D: Only the seniority changes, not the designation

e: MACPS grants financial upgradation only; there is no change in designation, duties or seniority.

q: A government servant joins a new post through proper channel. The pay he was drawing would place him above the maximum of the new level. Under pay protection, the excess is generally treated as:

options.B: Personal pay, to be absorbed in future increments
options.C: Pay forfeited from the date of joining

e: Pay protection is subject to the maximum of the new level; any excess, where the rules so provide, is treated as personal pay to be absorbed in future increments.

q:
Consider the following statements about MACPS:
I. Financial upgradations are granted on completion of 10, 20 and 30 years of service.
II. The prescribed APAR benchmark for MACPS is 'Very Good'.
III. A MACPS upgradation confers seniority in the higher level.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Statements I and II are correct. MACPS is purely financial and confers no seniority in the higher level.

q:
Consider the following statements about the option for fixation of pay on promotion:
I. The option must be exercised within one month of the date of promotion.
II. The option once exercised is final.
III. If no option is exercised in time, pay is fixed under FR 22(I)(a)(1) from the date of promotion.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: All three statements correctly state the option rules and the no-option default.

q:
Consider the following statements about stepping up of pay:
I. The senior and the junior must belong to the same cadre and hold identical posts in the lower and higher levels.
II. The anomaly must have arisen directly from fixation of pay on promotion under FR 22.
III. Stepping up is admissible even where the junior's higher pay is due to advance increments.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Statements I and II state the stepping-up conditions. An anomaly from advance increments or other causes outside FR 22 fixation does not qualify.

q:
Consider the following statements:
I. On first appointment, pay is normally fixed at the first cell (entry pay) of the level of the post.
II. A stagnation increment becomes due after every two years of service at the maximum of the level.
III. The Next Below Rule means fixation of pay at the next below stage of the Pay Matrix.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Statements I and II are correct. The Next Below Rule is about proforma promotion benefit for a servant away from the cadre, not a matrix stage.

q: What is the rate of the annual increment under the 7th CPC Pay Matrix?

options.C: 3% of basic pay, given effect by moving to the next cell of the level
options.D: One additional cell for every two years of service

e: The annual increment is 3% of basic pay, worked through movement to the next cell of the same level.

q: The only two dates of annual increment in a year are:

options.C: The anniversary of appointment and 1 January

e: There are only two increment dates, 1 January and 1 July; which one applies depends on the appointment/promotion window.

q: The prescribed APAR benchmark for grant of financial upgradation under MACPS is:
e: The MACPS benchmark is 'Very Good'; 'Good' is the benchmark for regular promotion.

q: The Modified Assured Career Progression Scheme was introduced in the era of the:
e: MACPS was introduced in the 6th CPC era to assure financial upgradations at 10, 20 and 30 years.

q: Shri A, in Level 6 at Rs 44,900, is promoted to a Level 7 post on 15-03-2026 and exercises no option. His pay fixed under FR 22(I)(a)(1) is:
e: One increment in Level 6 takes him notionally to Rs 46,200, and Level 7 has an equal cell at Rs 46,200.

q: In the same case, Shri A's annual increment date in the lower post is 1 July and within one month he opts for fixation from his date of next increment. His pay in Level 7 from 01-07-2026 will be:
e: On 01-07-2026 he first draws his annual increment to Rs 46,200 and then the promotional increment to Rs 47,600, fixing at the equal Level 7 cell.

q: Smt. B, in Level 5 at Rs 44,100, is granted her 2nd MACPS upgradation to Level 6 with effect from 10-09-2026. Her pay in Level 6 will be fixed at:
e: One increment in Level 5 gives Rs 45,400 notionally; Level 6 has no cell at Rs 45,400, so fixation is at the next cell above, Rs 46,200.

q: A servant is in Level 5 at Rs 44,100 and his date of annual increment is 1 July. His basic pay on 05-04-2026 and on 01-07-2026 respectively is:
e: Before the DNI the pre-increment pay of Rs 44,100 continues; on 01-07-2026 the increment takes him to the next Level 5 cell, Rs 45,400.

q: For the same servant (Level 5, Rs 44,100, increment date 1 July), his basic pay on 01-01-2027 will be:
e: His increment date is 1 July only, so nothing falls due on 1 January 2027; the pay drawn from 01-07-2026, Rs 45,400, continues.

q: Shri S (senior) was promoted to Level 7 and fixed at Rs 47,600. Shri J (junior, same cadre, identical posts) was later promoted to the same post and fixed at Rs 49,000 purely through FR 22 fixation. On stepping up, Shri S's pay becomes:
e: With all stepping-up conditions met, the senior's pay is raised to the junior's pay of Rs 49,000 in the higher level.

q: A servant is at the maximum of his level and his last increment in the level was Rs 2,700. On completing two years at the maximum, the stagnation increment granted to him is:
e: The stagnation increment is granted at the rate of the last increment drawn in the level, that is Rs 2,700.

q: An employee's pay has been fixed at Rs 47,600 in Level 7. Dearness Allowance payable on this pay at the rate in force from 1 January 2026 is:
e: DA at 60% of Rs 47,600 is Rs 28,560.

q: A servant in Level 5 at Rs 42,800 is promoted to a Level 6 post. Applying the two-step FR 22 method (Level 5 cells: 42,800 - 44,100; Level 6 cells: 43,600 - 44,900), his pay in Level 6 will be:
e: One increment in Level 5 gives Rs 44,100 notionally; Level 6 has no cell at Rs 44,100, so fixation is at the next cell above, Rs 44,900.

q: Which of the following statements about MACPS is NOT correct?

options.A: MACPS upgradations fall due on completion of 10, 20 and 30 years of service
options.B: A MACPS upgradation is treated as a regular promotion for seniority and all other purposes
options.C: Fixation on MACPS upgradation is done as on promotion, with one increment and fixation at the equal or next above cell
options.D: Cases for MACPS are considered by a Screening Committee on the basis of service records and APARs

e: MACPS is purely financial; it is not a promotion and confers no seniority in the higher level.

q: Which of the following statements about fixation of pay on promotion is NOT correct?

options.A: One increment is first granted in the existing level to locate the cell in the higher level
options.B: Fixation in the higher level is at the cell equal to the amount so arrived at, or the next cell above it
options.C: Pay is fixed directly at the minimum of the higher level, ignoring any increment in the lower level
options.D: The notional increment in the lower level is only a fixation device and is not actually drawn in that level

e: The two-step method must be followed; direct fixation at the higher level's minimum is a planted error.

q:
Assertion (A): On promotion, pay fixation first grants one increment in the existing (lower) level.
Reason (R): Pay in the higher level is then fixed at the cell equal to that amount, or the next cell above it.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R correctly explains A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

e: Both steps are correctly stated, but the second step describes what follows; it does not explain why the increment is granted first.

q:
Assertion (A): A servant promoted on 15 March draws his next annual increment on 1 January of the following year.
Reason (R): Promotions falling between 2 January and 1 July (both inclusive) take the next increment on 1 January of the following year.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R correctly explains A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

e: Both are true, and the two-date window rule in R directly explains the DNI in A.

q:
Assertion (A): The APAR benchmark prescribed for MACPS is 'Very Good'.
Reason (R): The APAR benchmark prescribed for regular promotion is 'Good'.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R correctly explains A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

e: Both benchmarks are correctly stated, but the promotion benchmark does not explain the MACPS benchmark; the pair is a contrast.

q:
Assertion (A): A senior employee can claim stepping up of pay with reference to a junior's financial upgradation under MACPS.
Reason (R): Stepping up is a remedy only for an anomaly arising directly from fixation of pay on promotion under FR 22.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R correctly explains A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

e: A is false because stepping up is not admissible against a junior's MACPS upgradation; R correctly states the scope of stepping up.

q:
Assertion (A): A stagnation increment becomes due after every two years of service at the maximum of the level.
Reason (R): A stagnation increment is treated as personal pay and counts for no purpose, not even pension.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R correctly explains A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

e: A is true; R is false because the stagnation increment is treated as pay for all purposes, including pensionary benefits.

q:
Assertion (A): On first appointment to a post, pay is normally fixed at the first cell (entry pay) of the level of the post.
Reason (R): Advance increments on initial fixation can be obtained by negotiation with the appointing authority.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R correctly explains A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

e: A is true; R is false because advance increments are admissible only where a specific rule or order provides for them, never by negotiation.

q:
Assertion (A): Pay fixation on a MACPS financial upgradation follows the same method as fixation on promotion.
Reason (R): On MACPS upgradation, one increment is granted in the existing level and pay is then fixed at the equal or next above cell in the higher level.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R correctly explains A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

e: Both are true, and R states the very method that A refers to, so R explains A.

q:
Assertion (A): An employee who opts for fixation from his date of next increment draws the higher-level pay from the date of promotion itself.
Reason (R): Till the date of next increment, an employee who has so opted draws the pay of the lower post.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R correctly explains A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

e: A is false because the higher-level pay begins only from the DNI under that option; R correctly states the interim position.

q:
Match the provision with its subject:
I. FR 22(I)(a)(1)
II. Next Below Rule
III. Date of Next Increment
IV. MACPS
a. 1 January or 1 July, fixed by the appointment/promotion window
b. Fixation of pay on promotion to a higher post
c. Proforma promotion benefit for a servant away on deputation when his junior is promoted
d. Financial upgradations at 10, 20 and 30 years of service
e: FR 22(I)(a)(1) governs promotion fixation; NBR protects the absent servant; DNI is 1 January or 1 July; MACPS gives upgradations at 10/20/30 years.

q:
Match the concept with its description:
I. Stepping up
II. Stagnation increment
III. Pay protection
IV. Screening Committee
a. Considers MACPS cases on the basis of service records and APARs
b. Brings a senior's pay at par with a junior's where FR 22 fixation created the anomaly
c. Granted after every two years at the maximum of the level, at the rate of the last increment
d. Fixation with reference to previous pay for a servant joining through proper channel
e: Stepping up cures an FR 22 anomaly; stagnation follows two years at the maximum; pay protection operates on proper-channel joining; the Screening Committee handles MACPS.
